morphology.capsule: Polysaccharide capsule in encapsulated strains (types a-f; type b historically most virulent)

habitat.hostAssociation: Obligate human commensal/pathogen; nasopharyngeal colonization common, especially with non-typeable strains
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Not found outside the human host

culture.media: Chocolate agar (requires both X [hemin] and V [NAD] factors); does not grow on plain blood agar
culture.growthCharacteristics: Facultative anaerobe, fastidious; grows better with 5-10% CO2
culture.colonyMorphology: Small, smooth, translucent colonies on chocolate agar

biochemicalTests.test: Satellite phenomenon around S. aureus streak

identificationClues: Grows on chocolate agar but not blood agar (requires X and V factors)
Satellite phenomenon around a Staphylococcus aureus streak on blood agar
Hib vaccine has dramatically reduced type b invasive disease

diseases: Meningitis (historically the leading cause in children before Hib vaccination)
Otitis media and sinusitis (typically non-typeable strains)
virulenceFactors: Polysaccharide capsule (type b — polyribosylribitol phosphate, PRP)
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: Hib conjugate vaccine has nearly eliminated invasive type b disease in vaccinated populations; non-typeable (unencapsulated) strains remain a common cause of otitis media and sinusitis
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Satellite phenomenon demonstrates the organism's dependence on factors V (NAD) supplied by hemolyzed staphylococcal colonies

examFacts.importantDisease: Meningitis (historically, pre-Hib vaccine), epiglottitis, otitis media
examFacts.importantTest: Satellite phenomenon; X/V factor requirement testing
examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Absolute requirement for both X (hemin) and V (NAD) factors, unlike most other Pasteurellaceae
